actions.description: Continue drafting the 90-day Economic Resilience Framework — advance from initial structure to a working draft with specific metric targets filled in. This tick the focus is on two of the four sections: (1) the retraining enrollment target — with 10 people enrolled this month (up from 6), I revise the 90-day target upward to 25 and document two specific bottlenecks I have identified: lack of awareness at the point of separation (workers learn about grants after they have already made other decisions) and the grant application process being routed through the municipal website rather than directly through Angela Wright's intake. Both are fixable. I write the fix into the framework. (2) The Gini trajectory target — with spending at 26 and employment at 50%, I set a specific and honest 90-day target: Gini improvement from 0.676 to 0.640, achievable only if the retraining pipeline accelerates and small business stabilization disbursements increase. I do not set aspirational numbers. I set numbers I can defend.
actions.expected_outcome: 90-day Economic Resilience Framework advances from announced commitment to working draft with two sections substantially complete. Sets the foundation for the remaining two sections (small business fund utilization and zoning recommendation) to be completed in the following tick.

actions.description: Meet directly with Lisa Freeman to acknowledge the Financial Triage Navigator she has launched at the community center. This is not a press release acknowledgment — it is a working conversation. I want to understand what cases she is seeing, what gaps in the existing programs the Navigator is surfacing, and whether there are specific bottlenecks she has identified that my framework can address. I also give her the explicit public acknowledgment I committed to in tick 10: I reference the Financial Triage Navigator by name in my next public communication as a concrete example of community-built response infrastructure that complements government programs. This costs me nothing and gives her concept institutional visibility.
actions.expected_outcome: Working relationship with Lisa Freeman established beyond public acknowledgment. Specific gap information from the Navigator feeds into the framework's bottleneck analysis. Public acknowledgment gives the Navigator visibility that may attract volunteer support or private funding.

actions.description: Issue a brief public statement acknowledging the employment rate at 50% and spending index at 26 as the current baseline the framework is responding to. The statement is not alarmist — it names the numbers, acknowledges they represent real hardship in Millfield, and directs anyone who needs immediate assistance to the Financial Triage Navigator at the community center and the small business stabilization grant program. I include the grant committee's direct contact rather than the municipal website URL. This redirects the routing failure I identified in tick 10. The protests have cooled, which means people are either hopeful or exhausted — I want to reach the ones who are still looking for a path.
actions.expected_outcome: Public communication that names current conditions accurately, directs people to existing resources with direct contact information, and demonstrates that the council is tracking the situation in real time rather than publishing reassurances. Potentially increases grant application volume and Navigator usage.

actions.description: Advance the municipal economic policy reading — push the retraining progress from 10% to 20%. The specific focus this month is on adaptive reuse zoning frameworks from other municipalities that have faced industrial or commercial property vacancies following economic disruption. Stephanie Morris's auto row data from the task force session identified the closing dealership property as a large-footprint opportunity. The framework needs a specific zoning recommendation with precedent from other localities. I find two or three examples of municipalities that have successfully rezoned former auto retail properties for delivery logistics, EV fleet servicing, or light industrial use. Those become the model for the Millfield recommendation.
actions.expected_outcome: Retraining progress advances from 10% to 20%. The adaptive reuse zoning section of the Economic Resilience Framework gains specific precedent cases and a draft recommendation. This is the section where my own skill development directly feeds the policy output I owe the community.

reasoning: Tick 11 context: employment at 50%, spending index at 26, Gini at 0.676, protests cooling, Financial Triage Navigator launched by community organizer. My savings are at approximately $49,953 after another $3,917 month of burn with no income — 12.8 months of runway, which is tighter than it was. The primary commitment of this tick is advancing the 90-day framework from announced to drafted. The framework is the deliverable I promised in a recorded public session. Nothing in this tick's inbox changes that priority. The Lisa Freeman association is important because she is doing the street-level work I cannot do from a policy seat — if her Navigator is surfacing gaps in my programs, I need to know what they are before the 90-day presentation, not after. The public statement on the employment and spending numbers is not optional: the community is watching whether I name conditions accurately or manage them. I name them. The retraining serves the framework directly — the zoning section needs precedent cases, and my self-directed study is finding them. Builder archetype: every action this tick builds something that will exist after the tick ends.
